| Category = Corn recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

A pleasantly-surprising recipe encountered in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|China]]. Also, a good first attempt for beginning deep-fryers. Makes a good substitute to chips or [[Cookbook:French Fries|fries]].

==Ingredients==

* Canned or frozen [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]]
* [[Cookbook:Egg Wash|Egg wash]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:MSG|MSG]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Spices and Herbs|Spices]] (as desired)
* [[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]]

==Procedure==

# If using frozen corn, thaw. If using canned corn, microwave in a glass bowl or gently heat on the stove until warm.
# Coat corn with a light layer of [[Cookbook:Egg Wash|egg wash]].
# Mix salt, pepper, MSG, and other spices into the flour.
# Move corn from the egg wash, and toss with the flour mixture until well-coated.
# Heat enough oil for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep-frying]] to moderate–high heat.
# Deep-fry floured corn until golden brown on the outside (less than 2 minutes).
# Serve as a complement to another dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Substitute moderately-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]] such as [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] and [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]] for additional flavors.

==Warnings==

* When a pot of hot oil catches fire, the flames will reach up to 2 or 3 feet. If you must work under flammable cabinets or shelves, be sure to have a fire extinguisher handy. An oil with a high [[Cookbook:Smoke Point|smoke point]] is less likely to cause problems, including indoor air pollution and fire. See [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Fry|deep-frying]] for more warnings.
